recap_lines: A dashboard's layout argues before anyone takes in a number.
State the question first, then pick position or length for quantity.
Aleatoric is chance in the data, epistemic is doubt about the data.
Label every error bar, and draw uncertainty at equal visual weight.
Truncated, inverted and inconsistent axes change the story, not the data.
An evidence-grade chart shows what could prove the claim wrong.
bookends.command: Quiz me on chart terms. Give me one short case at a time, a chart described in two sentences. I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold the answer until I reply. Draw on aleatoric uncertainty, epistemic uncertainty, truncated axes, axis inversion, inconsistent axes, cherry-picked window, missing baseline, selective uncertainty, and false precision.

beats.narration_text: The same three estimates, twice. On the left every interval is drawn, and A and B overlap. On the right B has no interval, so B looks plainly above A.
